f92.summary: Vincenzo I Gonzaga, Duke of Mantua, writes to his uncle Louis de Gonzague, duc de Nevers: he reports the rumour that Sixtus V was poisoned by the Spaniards, welcomes Henri IV's expected conversion, and assures Nevers (for the King) of his devotion to the French crown against the 'common enemy', a guarded pro-Bourbon declaration of September 1590. Deciphered with Nevers cipher no. 35 (BnF fr. 3995 f. 64).
f92.en:
17 September 1590. Most Illustrious and Most Excellent Lord, my most honoured Uncle,

I find myself owing an answer to four letters of Your Excellency, one of the 12th, another of the 27th, the third of
the 20th of July, and the last of the 6th of August, which I shall answer in order, begging you to excuse me if I
have been late in doing so; for the death of Our Lord [the Pope], which occurred on the 27th of last month at the 23rd
hour, has been the cause of it, since it seemed expedient to me that Your Excellency should be among the first
informed of the successor whom it will please God to give us.

system: Two-digit figures written unseparated: 11-40 letters with homophones, 41-99 words and names, plus overbarred figures and signs for titles and common words (Tomokiyo's Nevers no. 35, BnF fr. 3995 f. 64).
